author: Pallas, 1776

art.subject: Little Gull (Hydrocoloeus minutus), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage: white head with a dusky grey cap on the rear crown and a dark spot behind the eye; mantle and upperwing pale grey, the rounded wingtips pale grey and white without any black, with a white trailing edge; underwing blackish grey with a broad white trailing edge; body and tail white. Small black bill; dark eye; short dull red legs.
art.pose: flying low and buoyantly over the water, seen from slightly below, showing the dark underwing
art.scene: Korean river estuary in winter with calm grey water and mudflats; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Smallest gull, clearly smaller than the Black-headed Gull and close to a Common Tern in size; compact, with a rounded head and a short, fine bill much shorter than the head. Legs short, red. Wings rather short and broad with rounded tips; tail square. Flight buoyant and tern-like, dipping down to pick food from the water surface. In breeding plumage the whole head is black, without white eye crescents, and the bill dark red.
avoid: Do not paint black wingtips; the adult has no black in the wing (black tips mark the Black-headed and Saunders's Gulls).
Do not paint a white underwing; the adult underwing is blackish grey with a white rear edge.
Do not make it as big as a Black-headed Gull or give it a long bill.
Do not show the black breeding hood on a winter bird.
